title: Canary Circuit-Breaker & Policy Studio for Traffic Rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: As we onboard more customers to Dedicated and Private deployments, operations teams need an expressive but safe way to define canary rollouts, A/B experiments, shadowing, and automated rollback. Current rollout configs are limited to static step lists and ad-hoc guards. This ticket proposes a 'Policy Studio' component (config + runtime) that compiles declarative rollout specs into enforceable runtime guards: traffic split schedules, health-based circuit-breakers, probe shadowing, cohort-based A/B groups, and auto-rollback triggers.

Goals: 1) Provide a human-readable YAML/JSON DSL for step schedules and guard rules. 2) Enforce SLO-based circuit breakers (latency P95, error-rate, model divergence) with cooldowns and staged halting. 3) Support shadow traffic directives (percent of requests routed to shadow variant, sampling rules) that do not impact live split. 4) Enable A/B cohort selection (cookie/account attributes, random bucketing) with per-cohort metric capture. 5) Automatic rollback on sustained guard violations with audit trail and operator overrides.

High-level DSL example: 
```yaml
rollout: 
  name: "embedder-v2-canary"
  steps:
    - duration: 30m
      traffic: 5%
      checks:
        - type: sla
          metric: p95_latency_ms
          threshold: 120
          window: 5m
        - type: error_rate
          threshold: 0.02
          window: 5m
    - duration: 2h
      traffic: 25%
      shadow: 
        sample: 10%
      checks:
        - type: model-drift
          metric: semantic-similarity
          threshold: 0.88
          window: 15m
  rollback_policy:
    consecutive_violations: 3
    cooldown: 15m
    auto_rollback: true
  cohorts:
    - name: beta-users
      filter: "user.account_tier == 'beta'"
```

This ticket covers the config schema, rule compiler, runtime enforcement hooks, and a minimal Console surface for editing/previewing the compiled guards.
acceptance_criteria: A documented DSL (YAML) exists with at least: steps, traffic, shadow, checks, rollback_policy, cohorts
Runtime compiler converts DSL into a deterministic policy that can be injected into the router within < 500ms
Circuit-breaker rules trigger a staged halt and create an audit event captured in the Console timeline
Shadow directives correctly mirror sampled requests to shadow variants without changing client-visible responses
Auto-rollback performs a safe rollback, notifies on-call, and leaves a human-readable reason in the release history
design_decisions: Use a simple DSL instead of full policy language to reduce user errors and make drift reviewable
Evaluate two enforcement models: centralized policy agent vs per-pod interceptor. Start with per-route interceptor for faster iteration
Metric windows are configurable but have sensible defaults (5m for latency/error, 15m for drift) to avoid noisy flips
Automatic rollback requires a quorum: 3 consecutive evaluation windows or manual approval must be configurable via the policy
Cohort filters are evaluated in the request router using existing attribute extraction; heavy filters are offloaded to precomputed labels
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Schema + compiler + test harness. Output is a JSON policy blob with simple predicates and thresholds
Phase 2: Router integration: load policy blob via config service; per-request evaluation short-circuits on failing checks
Phase 3: Observability: wire checks to existing telemetry (metrics + traces). Add an audit index document to ES with policy events
Start with a proof-of-concept that supports latency and error-rate checks, then add model-drift and semantic checks as a follow-up
Ensure rollout controller supports safe roll-forward after transient failure; use cooldown timers and backoff increments
